ideas.title: Keyhold
ideas.cad_prompt:
ONE flat square board slab, 220 mm x 220 mm x 10 mm thick, forming a single fused body together with a fixed 7x7 grid of 49 square pedestal bosses raised from its top face. Each pedestal boss is 24 mm x 24 mm and stands exactly 3 mm proud of the slab's top surface. Every pair of laterally adjacent bosses is separated by a 4 mm gap of bare slab surface, so all 49 bosses read as 49 distinct stepped-up platforms, not a continuous raised plateau. The board with its 49 bosses is one part.

TWENTY Family-Single tiles, each a square block 22 mm x 22 mm x 8 mm. Reading around each tile's four side edges in order, the edges alternate tab, notch, tab, notch. Each tab edge bears one tooth, 10 mm wide and centered on the edge, protruding exactly 4 mm proud of the flat edge face. Each notch edge bears one matching cut, 10 mm wide and centered on the edge, recessed exactly 4 mm into the flat edge face. Where a tab edge of one Family-Single tile is placed flush against a notch edge of another Family-Single tile, the tooth is a snug removable friction-fit seat into the cut, with 0.2 mm clearance on each flank of the tooth (0.4 mm total), the tooth fully bottoming out against the base of the notch with no gap exceeding 0.4 mm anywhere along the seam.

TWENTY Family-Twin tiles, each a square block 22 mm x 22 mm x 8 mm, with the same tab-notch-tab-notch edge order as the Family-Single tiles. Each tab edge bears a pair of teeth, each tooth 4 mm wide, the two teeth separated by a 2 mm gap and centered together on the edge, both protruding exactly 4 mm proud of the flat edge face. Each notch edge bears the matching pair of cuts, each cut 4 mm wide with a 2 mm gap between them, centered together on the edge and recessed exactly 4 mm into the flat edge face. The fit between a Family-Twin tab pair and a Family-Twin notch pair uses the same 0.2 mm per-flank clearance and full seating as the Family-Single tiles.

A Family-Single edge and a Family-Twin edge never interlock: wherever a Family-Single tile's edge is placed against a Family-Twin tile's edge, or a tile's edge faces an empty pedestal, the two faces sit flush against each other (or against open air) with no tooth entering any cut.

SEPARATION, stated explicitly: all 40 tiles are individually loose, freestanding bodies. None of the 40 tiles is fused, welded, or otherwise joined to the board slab, and no tile is fused to any other tile. In the print layout, place the 40 tiles resting on top of their assigned pedestal bosses across the 7x7 grid, with a 0.2 mm vertical clearance gap between each tile's underside and the top face of its pedestal (a loose set-down fit, not a press fit). Wherever two tiles are not shown deliberately mated tab-into-notch, leave a minimum 2 mm lateral gap between their nearest edges so their bodies never touch. Counting the board (1 fused body) plus the 40 loose tiles, the assembly contains 41 distinct bodies.

Show several Family-Single and Family-Twin tiles seated on pedestals across the grid, with at least one pair of same-family tiles placed edge to edge so their tooth and cut are shown fully mated with no visible gap, and at least two further loose tiles lifted clear above their pedestals so the tab and notch edges on their perimeters are visible. Leave a number of pedestals empty. Render as a single uniform material, no color distinction, even studio lighting, sharp focus on the tooth and pedestal geometry.

unstated_in_spec: Per-tile arrangement of which of the 4 edges are tabs vs notches was not specified; assumed an alternating tab-notch-tab-notch pattern around each tile's perimeter, the most conservative reading that supports rotation-based mating on any side.

ideas.title: Twin Deck Solitaire
ideas.cad_prompt:
TWO identical cross-shaped boards (top board and bottom board), each 180 mm x 180 mm x 12 mm thick, in the standard 33-hole English peg-solitaire cross footprint. Each board is pierced with 33 holes, every hole 12 mm diameter and exactly 8 mm deep, arranged in the standard peg-solitaire cross pattern. The 33 hole positions on the top board are in true vertical alignment with the 33 hole positions on the bottom board, position for position, with a maximum lateral offset of 1.0 mm between any aligned pair, so each pair of aligned holes forms a real straight-through channel between the two boards.

The two boards are held in a fixed parallel stack, top board above bottom board, by FOUR corner support posts, one at each of the four matching corners of the cross footprint. Each post is a plain cylinder, 10 mm diameter, 60 mm long overall. Each end of each post carries a stepped-down insertion pin, 8 mm diameter x 15 mm long, that press-fits into a matching 8 mm diameter blind hole drilled 15 mm deep into the facing corner of each board, with 0.15 mm diametral interference for a permanent press fit. With both insertion pins fully seated, the two boards are held with their facing surfaces exactly 30 mm apart, leaving a clear open air gap of 30 mm between the two board bodies with nothing else connecting them. The two boards do not touch each other anywhere and are not fused into one body.

SIXTY-FOUR identical loose pegs, each a plain cylinder 11.4 mm diameter x 20 mm tall. Each peg is a snug, removable friction fit inside a 12 mm diameter hole, giving 0.3 mm radial clearance (0.6 mm diametral) between peg and hole wall -- tight enough that a peg standing in a hole stays seated under normal handling, loose enough to lift straight out by hand. No peg is fused to any board.

SEPARATION, stated explicitly: the 2 boards, 4 posts, and 64 pegs are 70 entirely separate bodies. No peg is fused to a board or to another peg; no post is fused to a board (the posts join the boards only through the press-fit insertion pins described above, which remain a distinct mechanical joint, not a monolithic merge). In the print layout, seat pegs upright in most holes on both boards, leave the center hole of the top board and the center hole of the bottom board empty, and show one additional peg suspended in the open 30 mm gap directly between one top-board hole and its aligned, empty bottom-board hole, positioned exactly on that hole's central axis with clear air space above and below it, touching neither board.

Render as a single uniform material, no color distinction, clean even studio lighting, camera angle low enough to show the open gap between the two boards clearly.

unstated_in_spec: Post total length (60mm) and stated air gap (30mm) are only mutually consistent if each post embeds into both boards via insertion pins; the spec did not state an insertion depth, so 15mm insertion into each board was inferred to reconcile the two given numbers.

Peg diameter conflicts across the spec: the components field and art_direction.scale both state pegs are 10mm diameter, while must_survive rank 5's fit-check thresholds specify a 11.4mm peg against a 12mm hole for a 0.3mm clearance. Used 11.4mm so the stated fit tolerance is met.

ideas.title: Eclipse
ideas.cad_prompt:
ONE flat square board slab, 220 mm x 220 mm x 12 mm thick, forming a single body with a fixed 8x8 grid of 64 shallow circular sockets sunk into its top face. Each socket is 24 mm diameter and 5 mm deep. Every pair of laterally adjacent sockets is separated by a 2 mm gap of solid board material, and the whole 8x8 grid is centered on the board with equal margins on all four sides (a 7 mm margin, computed from 8 sockets at 24 mm plus 7 gaps at 2 mm spanning 206 mm within the 220 mm board width).

SIXTY-FOUR identical reversible discs, each 23.4 mm diameter overall, a solid body of revolution. Each disc has a thin flat cylindrical rim running around its equator as a reference plane. One face of each disc is a smooth continuous dome that rises exactly 4 mm proud of the rim at its apex. The opposite face of the same disc is a smooth continuous dish that sinks exactly 4 mm below the rim at its lowest point. Measured along the disc's central axis from the dome's apex to the dish's floor, each disc is 8 mm thick overall. Every disc is identical; only the up-facing orientation differs from disc to disc.

FIT: each disc sits in a socket with 0.3 mm radial clearance (0.6 mm diametral) between the disc's 23.4 mm rim and the socket's 24 mm wall, a loose drop-in fit that lets the disc sit level and be lifted straight back out by hand in either orientation, dome-up or dish-up. With a disc seated dome-up, the dome apex sits 4 mm above the board's top face and the dish cavity on the underside does not touch the socket floor. With a disc seated dish-up, the dome on the underside points down into the socket and its apex clears the socket floor by 1 mm (5 mm socket depth minus 4 mm dome height). No seated disc touches the wall of its own socket or the body of any disc in a neighboring socket, since every socket is separated from its neighbors by the stated 2 mm gap of solid board material.

SEPARATION, stated explicitly: all 64 discs are individually loose, freestanding bodies, each entirely separate from the board and from every other disc. None of the 64 discs is fused, welded, or otherwise joined to the board or to any other disc. Counting the board (1 fused body, including its 64 sockets) plus the 64 loose discs, the assembly contains 65 distinct bodies.

In the print layout, seat discs in most of the 64 sockets across the grid, roughly half shown dome-up and half shown dish-up in a scattered mixed pattern, leave several sockets empty, and show one additional disc held just above an empty socket, tilted at an angle so both its dome face and its dish face are visible at once. Render as a single uniform material, no color distinction, raking studio light that makes the dome and dish relief read clearly across the grid.

unstated_in_spec: Disc diameter conflicts across the spec: components, art_direction.scale, and the hero_shot description all state discs are 24mm (matching the socket diameter exactly, i.e. zero clearance), while must_survive rank 4 requires a minimum 0.3mm clearance for the disc to be liftable. Reduced disc diameter to 23.4mm to satisfy the stated clearance requirement while keeping the socket at the literal 24mm diameter required by rank 3's opening-presence check.
